title: Why did the Philippines take back Subic Bay from America?
fullText: in 1992  the largest American military base outside America wasn't in Germany and it wasn't in Japan it was the Subic Bay in the Philippines a naval installation roughly the size of Singapore and within the year the US Navy had lowered its flag and sailed away not because it lost a war  because it lost a vote which raises the obvious question why did the Philippines take back Subic Bay and more to the point  why did the country with the most aircraft carriers on earth get evicted by a country with none the answer involves a volcano a typhoon and a single show of hands so in 1898 the United States took the Philippines from Spain  and then having arrived as liberators governed it as a colony for the next five decades a distinction the Filipinos were assured was very important independence came in 1946  with paperwork attached a 1947 agreement leasing America its bases built partly on land taken from the indigenous Aitar people who were compensated with nothing  for 99 years a 1966 renegotiation then trimmed that lease to 25 years quietly moving the expiry date  from 2046 all the way up to 1991 meanwhile American money and weapons helped keep the dictator Ferdinand Marcos comfortable through 14 years of martial law then in 1986 Filipinos overthrew him and replaced his rule book with a new constitution buried in it were two trip wires no nuclear weapons on Philippine soil and no new bases treaty without 16 of the Senate's 23 votes remember both which brings us to June 15th, 1991 when with the lease expiring and negotiators mid haggle Mount Pinatubo produced the second largest volcanic eruption of the 20th century on the very day a typhoon made landfall the rain mixed the ash into wet concrete which then landed on both American bases collapsing roofs by the dozen Washington surveyed Clark Air Base  ran the numbers and filed the second largest eruption of the century under maintenance issue unresolvable Clark was abandoned now you might assume the volcano had settled the whole question  it hadn't  Subic survived and a deal for 10 more years there was still on the table the base's fate wouldn't be decided by Laura but by 23 senators and here the story stops cooperating because the loudest voice for keeping the American military was President Corazon Aquino  yes that Corazon Aquino the woman who overthrew the American backed dictator who warned that losing the bases would flatten an already battered economy and personally marched on the Senate with around 100,000 supporters to say so the poles backed her too with the president the public and the world's last superpower all pushing one way ratification was a formality it was not a formality so why did the Senate actually vote America out well the first reason was memory several of the senators were human rights lawyers and they knew precisely whose money had bankrolled Marcos's martial law to them this wasn't a defence policy question so much as an unpaid invoice also Washington had armed them US policy was to neither confirm nor deny nuclear weapons on its bases which is a difficult answer to give a country whose constitution banned the things and beyond this with the Soviet Union dissolving even Washington doubted the base was worth the price it refused to raise its offer and would sooner leave than haggle so after days of floor debate on September 16th, 1991 the Senate voted galleries full crowds pressed against the gates outside 23 senators a show of hands  and the count came back level  11 - 11 the largest overseas base on earth and the vote had cancelled itself out leaving one hand still down the Senate President Hovito Solonga  himself one of those human rights lawyers he voted no 12 - 11 the treaty was defeated inside the chamber applause and tears  outside singing and on the floor 91 year old retired Senator Lorenzo Tan Yada whose own son had filed the motion that killed the treaty pushed himself up out of his wheelchair shouting Mabuhay  long live the Philippines the press would call the 12 the magnificent 12 but Solonga's raised hand was never a gamble the treaty had needed 16 yes votes and it never had them the Constitution had already written the verdict he simply delivered it  Aquino tried one final move a national referendum to overrule her own Senate which promptly buckled under its legal problems so the withdrawal began  and on November 24th, 1992 the flag over Subic came down for the last time the final 1,416 sailors and Marines departed aboard the USS Bello Wood closing out 94 years of American military presence the departing admiral told the crowd it wasn't goodbye just farewell for now we hope to come back as soon as we can about that within roughly three years China had occupied Mischief Reef  comfortably inside waters the Philippines claims  and kept building Manila now examining a superpower shaped gap in its coastline began inviting the Americans back a 2014 agreement put US troops onto Philippine bases expanded to nine sites by 2,023 including around Subic Bay  so today there are American forces once again  at the bay the size of Singapore only now they're guests on Philippine soil under Philippine terms  removable by request which is a procedure the Philippines can confirm works as for the standoff over those reefs that's a whole other episode
